comment_text: You are looking at the economics wrong.  On average, a major studio film has an advertising budget roughly equal to the production budget.  And the studio only get half of the box office with the theater keeping the other half.  So a film has to make at the box office 4 times the production budget in order to break even during the initial run.  Now, or course there is some give here, as the studio makes more downstream of the box office (VOD, streaming licensing, and in a prior era VHS sales),  But for the original movie, there were no obvious ancillary income streams (before VOD, VHS, or obviously streaming) other than it randomly running on UHF channel.  I think you have it count the triangle movie as a wash - not a flop, but it barely made money when the full accounting is considered.
